name: Isolated Cryptophthalmia

criteria.description: Complete or partial absence of the palpebral fissure with skin covering the eyeball
Absent or severely malformed globe (anophthalmia or microphthalmia) without other systemic anomalies
No evidence of systemic or syndromic involvement differentiating isolated cryptophthalmia from syndromic forms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent or malformed palpebral fissure with absent or malformed globe in the absence of systemic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and exclusion of syndromic conditions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete or partial absence of palpebral fissure
searchTerms: missing or very small eye opening

common.symptomName: Skin continuous over the eyeball without eyelid formation
searchTerms: eyeball covered by skin instead of eyelid
no eyelid formation, skin continuous over eye
lack of normal tear drainage structures
improperly formed muscles controlling eye movement

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial asymmetry due to orbital hypoplasia
Mild skin scarring or contracture around the eye region

rare.symptomName: Secondary glaucoma in residual ocular tissue
Mild developmental delay due to visual impairment
searchTerms: slow development due to poor vision
mild learning delay from vision problems

rare.symptomName: Epiphora due to lacrimal drainage anomalies
searchTerms: watery eyes from blocked tear ducts

imaging: Orbital ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic globe
MRI or CT scan demonstrating absence of palpebral fissure and ocular structures
genetic: Mutations in genes related to ocular development such as FOXE3, PITX2 (in some cases)
Mostly sporadic but rare familial cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing absence of eyelids and palpebral fissure
Exclusion of systemic syndromes by clinical and genetic evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic anomalies such as limb defects, craniofacial abnormalities
Eyelid fusion with ectodermal dysplasia features

redFlags: Complete absence of eyelids with skin covering the globe
Severe visual impairment or blindness at birth
Presence of associated systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Verma AS, Fitzpatrick DR. Anophthalmia and microphthalmia. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007
